questions.question: What does adding a `loading.tsx` file next to a `page.tsx` do?
options: Automatically wraps the route in a Suspense boundary, shown instantly on navigation before the page's data finishes loading
Disables server rendering for that route
questions.explanation: loading.tsx is a file convention that Next.js automatically turns into a Suspense fallback for that route segment — no manual boundary code needed.

questions.question: In a page with one fast section and one slow section, what does wrapping only the slow section in `<Suspense>` achieve?
options: The whole page waits for the slow section anyway
The fast section renders and streams to the browser immediately, while the slow section's fallback shows until its data resolves
It disables caching for the whole page
It converts the fast section into a Client Component
questions.explanation: Suspense boundaries let Next.js stream independent parts of a page separately — fast content doesn't wait on slow content elsewhere on the same page.

questions.question: Compared to a traditional client-side spinner (fetch-after-hydration), what's the advantage of Suspense-based streaming?
options: Data fetching starts on the server immediately, and resolved HTML streams in already-rendered, without waiting for JS to hydrate first
Suspense makes the JavaScript bundle smaller
It removes the need for a database
questions.explanation: A client-fetched spinner requires sending an empty shell, hydrating, then fetching. Streaming starts the server-side fetch immediately and sends real rendered HTML as it resolves.

questions.question: Once the fallback in a `<Suspense>` boundary is replaced with real content, does the browser need to re-fetch that data client-side?
options: No — the server streams the already-rendered HTML for that boundary directly, no separate client-side refetch is needed
Only if the component is a Client Component
questions.explanation: The resolved content arrives as part of the same streamed server response, swapping out the fallback in place without an additional round trip.
